s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: to cause someone to be well-disposed toward or to be pleased with someone
s.g: to cause to be pleased; to please

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: pertaining to that which causes someone to be pleased

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: pertaining to that which causes someone to be pleased

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian who sent greetings in {S:05500402100014}

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to having high status, with the possible implication of special family relations contributing to such status
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 1:26|1 Corinthians 1:26⟧, it is somewhat unlikely, though not impossible, that hereditary status is involved.

s.dp: Learn › Be Willing To Learn
s.d: a willingness to learn and evaluate something fairly
s.g: willingness to learn; to be open-minded; to be noble-minded

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Weather
s.d: sunny, mild weather without strong winds
s.c: Fair weather may be referred to by a number of different expressions, for example, ‘growing weather’ or ‘cloudless skies’ or ‘happy weather.’ The variety of expressions depends largely upon the type of activity associated with weather or the atmospheric conditions typical of what people regard as fair weather. In a number of languages fair weather is expressed as a negative of bad weather, that is to say, ‘a not stormy day’ or ‘a not windy day.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: to be pleased with something or someone, with the implication of resulting pleasure
s.g: to be pleased with; to take pleasure in

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: to take pleasure in something in that it fulfills one’s desires
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to enjoy’ is ‘to make someone happy’ or ‘to make one feel good.’ This expression in ⟦2 Thessalonians 2:12|2 Thessalonians 2:12⟧ may be rendered as ‘but when they are sinning, they feel good’ or ‘but to sin makes them happy.’

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to think of something as being good, better, or preferable
s.g: to choose as better; to prefer; to seem good to

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: that which pleases someone

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire, Want, Wish
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐδοκέω<SDBG:εὐδοκέω:000002>}[c] ‘to prefer,’ {D:30.97}) that which is desired on the basis of its appearing to be beneficial

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Goodness
s.d: doing that which is good and beneficial to someone

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Goodness
s.d: to do that which is good and beneficial to someone

s.dp: Help, Care For › Help
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐεργετέω<SDBG:εὐεργετέω:000000>} ‘to do good to,’ {D:88.7}) a person who provides important help or assistance, often occurring as a title for princes or distinguished persons

s.dp: Proper, Improper
s.d: pertaining to being fitting or appropriate, with the probable implication of usable

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to being capable of being put to a useful purpose

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time immediately subsequent to a previous point of time (the actual interval of time differs appreciably, depending upon the nature of the events and the manner in which the sequence is interpreted by the writer)
s.c: It is impossible to determine from the context whether εὐθέως in ⟦3 John 1:14|3 John 1:14⟧ should be understood as referring to a very short lapse of time and therefore be rendered as ‘very soon,’ or whether it refers to the very next event which is relevant to the total context.

s.dp: Maritime Activities
s.d: to follow a straight course to one’s destination or goal
s.g: to sail a straight course; to sail straight to

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Encouragement, Consolation
s.d: to be or to become encouraged and hence cheerful
s.g: to be encouraged; to take courage; to become encouraged
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to become encouraged’ is ‘to have one’s heart return’ or ‘to have one’s liver stand up again’ or ‘to have one’s heart become hard again.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Encouragement, Consolation
s.d: pertaining to being encouraged

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Encouragement, Consolation
s.d: pertaining to being encouraged

s.dp: Features of Objects › Straight, Crooked
s.d: to make something straight
s.g: to cause to be straight; to make straight; to straighten
s.c: In a number of languages a distinction is made between making some object straight and straightening out a road. The first meaning may be equivalent to ‘bending something straight,’ while the latter meaning may be literally ‘to avoid the curves.’

s.dp: Maritime Activities
s.d: to steer a ship on its course
s.g: to pilot a ship; to steer a course
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘piloting a ship’ is ‘to hold the rudder’ or ‘to hold the wheel’ (referring to the wheel which controls the position of the rudder).

s.dp: Features of Objects › Straight, Crooked
s.d: pertaining to being straight in contrast to what is crooked{N:001}

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Just, Righteous
s.d: pertaining to being just and right

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Just, Righteous
s.d: (an idiom, literally: a straight road) the right or correct pattern of behavior
s.g: right way; correct manner of life; just way of life

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time immediately subsequent to a previous point of time (the actual interval of time differs appreciably, depending upon the nature of the events and the manner in which the sequence is interpreted by the writer)
s.c: In ⟦Mark 1:21|Mark 1:21⟧ εὐθύς probably implies what was done on the immediately following Sabbath. Accordingly, one may translate this expression in ⟦Mark 1:21|Mark 1:21⟧ as ‘and on the next Sabbath he went into the synagogue and taught.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Just, Righteous
s.d: the quality of uprightness
s.c: In a number of languages it makes no sense to speak of a ‘righteous scepter,’ and therefore this expression in ⟦Hebrews 1:8|Hebrews 1:8⟧ may be better rendered as ‘you will rule righteously’ or ‘the way in which you rule is just.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: to experience an appropriate occasion for some activity
s.g: to have an appropriate time for; to have an occasion to; to have a chance to

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to spend time in an enjoyable and profitable manner
s.g: to spend time; to enjoy spending time

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: a favorable occasion for some event

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: pertaining to being a favorable occasion for some event

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: pertaining to being a favorable occasion for some event

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Easy, Light
s.d: (occurring only in the comparative form in the NT) pertaining to that which is easy, in the sense of not requiring great effort or work
s.c: In some languages it is difficult to render in a succinct manner an expression such as ‘easier to do,’ for a comparative expression involving degree of effort may require complex restructuring. Accordingly, one can often translate the first part of this expression in ⟦Matthew 19:24|Matthew 19:24⟧ as ‘a camel does not have to struggle as much to go through the eye of a needle as …’

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: to show reverent regard for
s.g: to reverence; reverent regard for; reverence
s.c: In εὐλαβέομαι and εὐλάβεια there is also a certain element of awe, which may be interpreted in some instances as implying even fear. The implication of such reverent fear or awe is, of course, obedience, and some scholars prefer to interpret these terms in ⟦Hebrews 11:7|Hebrews 11:7⟧ and ⟦Hebrews 5:7|Hebrews 5:7⟧ as meaning ‘to obey’ (see LN 36.13) or ‘obedience.’

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: to show reverent regard for
s.g: to reverence; reverent regard for; reverence
s.c: In εὐλαβέομαι and εὐλάβεια there is also a certain element of awe, which may be interpreted in some instances as implying even fear. The implication of such reverent fear or awe is, of course, obedience, and some scholars prefer to interpret these terms in ⟦Hebrews 11:7|Hebrews 11:7⟧ and ⟦Hebrews 5:7|Hebrews 5:7⟧ as meaning ‘to obey’ (see LN 36.13) or ‘obedience.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Obey, Disobey
s.d: to obey, with the implication of awe and reverence for the source of a command
s.c: For another interpretation of εὐλαβέομαι in ⟦Hebrews 11:7|Hebrews 11:7⟧, see εὐλαβέομαι LN 53.7.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: pertaining to being reverent toward God

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: to speak of something in favorable terms
s.g: to praise; to speak well of

s.dp: Communication › Bless, Curse
s.d: to ask God to bestow divine favor on, with the implication that the verbal act itself constitutes a significant benefit{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of ‘to bless’ is ‘to pray God on behalf of’ or ‘to ask God to do something good for.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: to provide benefits, often with the implication of certain supernatural factors involved
s.g: to act kindly toward; to bless
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 1:3|Ephesians 1:3⟧ there is an obvious play on the words εὐλογητός and εὐλογήσας. The term εὐλογητός designates ‘the one to be praised’ (see LN 33.362), but εὐλογήσας designates ‘blessing.’

s.dp: Communication › Bless, Curse
s.d: to ask God to bestow divine favor on, with the implication that the verbal act itself constitutes a significant benefit{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of ‘to bless’ is ‘to pray God on behalf of’ or ‘to ask God to do something good for.’

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐλογέω<SDBG:εὐλογέω:000000>}[a] ‘to praise,’ {D:33.356}) pertaining to being worthy of praise or commendation

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: to speak of something in favorable terms
s.g: to praise; to speak well of

s.dp: Communication › Flatter
s.d: excessive praise
s.c: In some languages flattery is expressed in a descriptive manner, for example, ‘to say that a person is wonderful when he really isn’t.’ Sometimes flattery is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to use big words about a small person’ or ‘to call a donkey a man.’

s.dp: Communication › Bless, Curse
s.d: to ask God to bestow divine favor on, with the implication that the verbal act itself constitutes a significant benefit
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of ‘to bless’ is ‘to pray God on behalf of’ or ‘to ask God to do something good for.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐλογέω<SDBG:εὐλογέω:000002>}[c] ‘to bless,’ {D:88.69}) the content of the act of blessing
s.c: In ⟦Romans 15:29|Romans 15:29⟧ this blessing is something which Christ has extended to Paul, in other words, a type of special favor granted to Paul by Christ.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐλογέω<SDBG:εὐλογέω:000001>}[b] ‘to bless,’ {D:33.470}) that which is bestowed or given as a blessing or benefit

s.dp: Quantity › Abundance, Excess, Sparing
s.d: (an idiom, literally: on the basis of blessings) a large amount of something, with the implication of blessing or benefit
s.c: In translating ⟦2 Corinthians 9:6|2 Corinthians 9:6⟧ it may be necessary to indicate clearly the objects which form the abundance, for example, ‘the one who plants a great deal of grain will reap a very large crop.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: pertaining to being generous in sharing

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the mother of Timothy

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to consider a view favorably, with the intention of finding a solution
s.g: to consider someone’s views in a favorable light; to consider how to solve
s.c: For other interpretations of εὐνοέω in ⟦Matthew 5:25|Matthew 5:25⟧, see LN 31.20 and LN 56.3.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to come to an agreement with someone
s.g: to agree to; to agree with
s.c: For other interpretations of εὐνοέω in ⟦Matthew 5:25|Matthew 5:25⟧, see LN 30.23 and LN 56.3.

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Lawsuit, Case
s.d: to settle a case out of court
s.c: For other interpretations of εὐνοέω in ⟦Matthew 5:25|Matthew 5:25⟧, see LN 30.23 and LN 31.20.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
s.d: a state of zeal based upon a desire to be involved in some activity or state
s.c: An equivalent of ‘serve wholeheartedly’ (⟦Ephesians 6:7|Ephesians 6:7⟧) may be expressed in some languages as ‘serve because you really want to’ or ‘serve because that is what you really desire to do.’

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐνοῦχος<SDBG:εὐνοῦχος:000000>}[a] ‘eunuch,’ {D:9.25}) to cause a person to be a eunuch
s.g: to make a eunuch; to castrate
s.c: Sometimes one may render εὐνουχίζω as ‘to cause a person not to be able to have marital relations.’|In a number of languages the castration of a man is referred to by a term very different from what is employed in the case of the castration of an animal.

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: (used with a reflexive pronoun) to live without engaging in sexual relations
s.g: to be celibate; to live without marrying

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: a castrated male person{N:001}
s.c: In the ancient Middle East eunuchs were frequently in charge of royal harems and sometimes rose to high positions of state. The reference to the eunuch in ⟦Acts 8:34|Acts 8:34⟧ is best interpreted as ‘court official’ (see LN 37.85).|Since in many societies castration of human males is not known, any attempt to employ a descriptive explanation within the text might seem unnecessarily crude and even vulgar. A number of translators have therefore preferred to borrow a term for eunuch and then place the explanation of its meaning in a glossary or word list.

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: a human male who without being castrated is by nature incapable of sexual intercourse{N:001}

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: a male person who abstains from marriage without being necessarily impotent{N:001}

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: an official of an Oriental court who was entrusted with various important responsibilities and who was also a eunuch
s.c: In a context such as ⟦Acts 8:34|Acts 8:34⟧, the focus of meaning of εὐνοῦχος seems to be upon the person’s official responsibilities and position rather than upon his physical condition. It may therefore be more in keeping with the context to employ an expression such as ‘official of the court’ or ‘important official.’ On the other hand, in view of a eunuch’s limited acceptance in Jewish religion, the mention of the physical condition would fit Luke’s theological purposes well.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian woman in the church of Philippi

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Favorable Circumstances or State
s.d: to experience and enjoy favorable circumstances
s.g: to get along well; to succeed
s.c: In a number of languages εὐοδόομαι in ⟦3 John 1:2|3 John 1:2⟧ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to always eat well’ or ‘to live under the shade’ or ‘to live always with laughter and song.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of εὐοδόομαι ‘to travel along a good road,’ not occurring in the NT) to be successful in acquiring profit or gain
s.g: to prosper; to gain in business; to gain by work

s.dp: Aspect › Complete, Finish, Succeed
s.d: to be successful in accomplishing some activity or event

s.dp: Religious Activities › Roles and Functions
s.d: devoted service to God
s.g: devoted to; devoted service of; devotion

s.dp: Communication › Urge, Persuade
s.d: pertaining to being easily persuaded, with the implication of being open to reason or willing to listen
s.g: one who is easily persuaded; open to reason

s.dp: Control, Rule › Control, Restrain
s.d: pertaining to the exertion of tight control
s.g: being in control of; controlling tightly

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Goodness
s.d: doing that which is good and beneficial to someone

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be Rich, Be Wealthy
s.d: to be financially well off
s.g: to have plenty; to be rich; to be well off
s.c: It may be useful in some languages to translate εὐπορέομαι in ⟦Acts 11:29|Acts 11:29⟧ as ‘each one was to do this in proportion as he had more than he needed’ or ‘… in proportion to the amount of possessions which he owned.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be Rich, Be Wealthy
s.d: the result of having acquired wealth
s.c: It may also be convenient to translate this clause in ⟦Acts 19:25|Acts 19:25⟧ as ‘you know that this work we do makes us rich.’ For another interpretation of εὐπορία in ⟦Acts 19:25|Acts 19:25⟧, see εὐπορία LN 57.201.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: an easy means of gaining a profit from one’s business or trade
s.g: good business; easy way of making a living
s.c: For another interpretation of εὐπορία LN 57.32.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: a state of beauty or fine appearance, with the implication of being attractive and well-suited

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: pertaining to that which is particularly acceptable, and hence quite pleasing
s.c: In some languages the statement ‘an offering very acceptable to God’ (⟦Romans 15:16|Romans 15:16⟧) must be rendered as ‘an offering with which God is very pleased’ or ‘an offering which pleases God very much.’

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Favorable Circumstances or State
s.d: pertaining to that which is particularly favorable or propitious

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Hypocrisy, Pretense
s.d: to make a good showing, particularly with regard to outward appearances
s.g: to wish to show off; to make a good showing

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Wind
s.d: a hybrid formation from Greek and Latin, meaning literally either ‘east wind’ or ‘broad wind’: a strong storm wind blowing from the northeast
s.c: It is, of course, possible to use the form Εὐρακύλων as a proper name, but this is probably much less meaningful than employing a term such as ‘strong northeast wind’ or ‘a strong storm coming from the northeast.’ In instances in which languages do not readily and easily distinguish between north and northeast or between east and northeast, it may be satisfactory simply to use a term such as ‘east,’ but frequently one can use a designation for ‘northeast’ such as ‘between the north and the east’ or ‘a little to the north of east.’

s.dp: Learn › Learn the Location of Something
s.d: to learn the location of something, either by intentional searching or by unexpected discovery
s.g: to learn the whereabouts of something; to find; to discover; to come upon; to happen to find

s.dp: Learn
s.d: to learn something previously not known, frequently involving an element of surprise
s.g: to learn; to find out; to discover

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to attain a state, with the supplementary implication of discovery

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to begin to experience an event or state
s.g: to begin to experience; to come into an experience; to attain

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to be in a state which has not been anticipated{N:002}
s.g: to be found to be; to discover to be; to turn out to be

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › Narrow, Wide
s.d: pertaining to being broad and spacious, with the implication of agreeable and pleasant

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: appropriate beliefs and devout practice of obligations relating to supernatural persons and powers
s.c: In a number of languages there is no specific term equivalent to ‘religion,’ but one may always speak of this phase of culture by some phrase such as ‘how to act toward God’ or ‘what one does to placate spirits’ or ‘how one worships.’

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: behavior reflecting correct religious beliefs and attitudes
s.c: In a number of languages εὐσέβεια in ⟦1 Timothy 2:2|1 Timothy 2:2⟧ may be appropriately translated as ‘to live as God would have us live’ or ‘to live as God has told us we should live.’

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: to express in attitude and ritual one’s allegiance to and regard for deity
s.c: In a number of languages worship is expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bow down before,’ ‘to lower one’s head before,’ ‘to raise one’s arms to,’ ‘to sing to,’ ‘to honor.’ It is important in selecting an expression for worship to employ a term or phrase which will include various aspects of worship.

s.dp: Mode › Should, Ought
s.d: to fulfill one’s socio-religious obligations
s.g: to fulfill one’s duties; to complete one’s religious duty

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: pertaining to being devoted to a proper expression of religious beliefs{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of ‘living a godly life’ may be best expressed as ‘to live as God would have one live’ or ‘to live like one should who believes in God’ or ‘to always do what God requires.’ In some languages, however, the only equivalent is ‘to live a good life’ or ‘to live always doing good to others.’ The shift from the focus upon religious belief to good living or being good to others results from the fact that in some religious systems there is little or no connection between religious beliefs and moral behavior.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: pertaining to being devoted to a proper expression of religious beliefs{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of ‘living a godly life’ may be best expressed as ‘to live as God would have one live’ or ‘to live like one should who believes in God’ or ‘to always do what God requires.’ In some languages, however, the only equivalent is ‘to live a good life’ or ‘to live always doing good to others.’ The shift from the focus upon religious belief to good living or being good to others results from the fact that in some religious systems there is little or no connection between religious beliefs and moral behavior.

s.dp: Understand › Ease or Difficulty in Understanding
s.d: pertaining to being easily understood

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to being affectionate and compassionate

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Modesty, Propriety
s.d: pertaining to being a fitting or becoming manner of behavior
s.g: in a becoming manner; decently; with propriety

s.dp: Proper, Improper
s.d: pertaining to being proper, with the implication of pleasing

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: a state of beauty or fine appearance, with the implication of being attractive and well-suited

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: pertaining to having an attractive form

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to having special prestige or honor

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: a relatively high point on a scale of extent and implying tension and opposition{N:001}

s.dp: Communication › Language Levels
s.d: coarse jesting involving vulgar expressions and indecent content

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a young man who fell out of a window in Troas

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: speaking of something in favorable terms

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐφημία<SDBG:εὐφημία:000000>} ‘to praise,’ {D:33.356}) pertaining to deserving approval or good reputation
s.g: worthy of praise; worthy of approval
s.c: In a number of languages ‘worthy of praise’ may be rendered as ‘what people should praise.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Ripen, Produce Fruit, Bear Seed
s.d: to produce an abundance of good fruit or grain
s.g: to yield plenty of fruit; to produce a good harvest
s.c: In some languages it may be difficult, if not impossible, to speak of the ground producing crops (⟦Luke 12:16|Luke 12:16⟧). Therefore, one may employ such expressions as ‘good crops grew on the ground’ or ‘the plants produced plenty of fruit’ or ‘… plenty of grain.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: to cause someone to be or become happy or glad
s.g: to make glad; to cheer up; to cause to be happy

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: to rejoice as an expression of happiness
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to translate εὐφραίνομαι in ⟦Acts 2:26|Acts 2:26⟧ in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘my heart sings’ or ‘my heart shouts because it is happy.’ For another interpretation of εὐφραίνομαι in ⟦Acts 7:41|Acts 7:41⟧, see LN 51.3.

s.dp: Festivals
s.d: to celebrate an occasion, with the implication of happiness and joy
s.c: For another interpretation of εὐφραίνομαι in ⟦Acts 7:41|Acts 7:41⟧, see LN 25.122.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a river in Mesopotamia

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: a state of joyful happiness

s.dp: Communication › Thanks
s.d: to express gratitude for benefits or blessings
s.c: Thanks is often expressed in highly idiomatic ways. For example, in some languages one says thank you by saying ‘may God pay you.’ Such a phrase may be so standardized as to even be used in expressing thankfulness to God himself. In other instances, thankfulness may be expressed as ‘you have made my heart warm.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Thankful, Grateful
s.d: to be thankful on the basis of some received benefit
s.g: to be thankful; to be grateful

s.dp: Communication › Thanks
s.d: expressing gratitude for benefits or blessings
s.c: Thanks is often expressed in highly idiomatic ways. For example, in some languages one says thank you by saying ‘may God pay you.’ Such a phrase may be so standardized as to even be used in expressing thankfulness to God himself. In other instances, thankfulness may be expressed as ‘you have made my heart warm.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Thankful, Grateful
s.d: pertaining to being thankful for what has been done to or for someone
s.c: Expressions for ‘thankfulness’ are frequently idiomatic, for example, ‘to have a full heart’ or ‘to speak from the heart’ or even ‘to say, You are very kind.’ For another interpretation of εὐχάριστος in ⟦Colossians 3:15|Colossians 3:15⟧, see LN 33.352.

s.dp: Communication › Thanks
s.d: (derivative of {L:εὐχαριστέω<SDBG:εὐχαριστέω:000000>}[a] ‘to thank,’ {D:33.349}) pertaining to expressing thanks
s.c: For another interpretation of εὐχάριστος in ⟦Colossians 3:15|Colossians 3:15⟧, see LN 25.99.

s.dp: Communication › Pray
s.d: the act of speaking to or making requests of God{N:001}
s.c: In some languages there are a number of different terms used for prayer depending upon the nature of the content, for example, requests for material blessing, pleas for spiritual help, intercession for others, thanksgiving, and praise. There may also be important distinctions on the basis of urgency and need. The most generic expression for prayer may simply be ‘to speak to God.’ It is normally best to avoid an expression which means primarily ‘to recite.’

s.dp: Communication › Swear, Put Under Oath, Vow
s.d: a promise to God that one will do something, with the implication that failure to act accordingly will result in divine sanctions against the person in question
s.c: It may, however, be necessary in some languages to be somewhat more specific in rendering ‘vow,’ so that one may need to translate this expression in ⟦Acts 21:23|Acts 21:23⟧ as ‘there are four men here who have promised God that they will do something.’

s.dp: Communication › Pray
s.d: to speak to or to make requests of God{N:001}
s.g: to pray; to speak to God; to ask God for; prayer
s.c: In some languages there are a number of different terms used for prayer depending upon the nature of the content, for example, requests for material blessing, pleas for spiritual help, intercession for others, thanksgiving, and praise. There may also be important distinctions on the basis of urgency and need. The most generic expression for prayer may simply be ‘to speak to God.’ It is normally best to avoid an expression which means primarily ‘to recite.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire, Want, Wish
s.d: to desire something, with the implication of a pious wish

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to being of positive or good use

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Encouragement, Consolation
s.d: to be or to become encouraged and hence cheerful
s.g: to be encouraged; to take courage; to become encouraged
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to become encouraged’ is ‘to have one’s heart return’ or ‘to have one’s liver stand up again’ or ‘to have one’s heart become hard again.’

s.dp: Features of Objects › Fragrance, Odor
s.d: a pleasant or sweet-smelling odor
s.c: Since the reference in ⟦Philippians 4:18|Philippians 4:18⟧ is to a sacrifice, the use of εὐωδία may seem strange, if not contradictory, in many languages, since the odor from burning flesh is normally not regarded as being fragrant or pleasant. It may therefore be necessary to include a marginal note to explain this usage.

s.dp: Spacial Orientations › Left, Right, Straight Ahead, Opposite
s.d: pertaining to being to the left of some point of reference

s.dp: Linear Movement › Jump, Leap
s.d: to leap or jump onto a place or object
s.g: to jump on; to leap upon

s.dp: Number › Once, Twice, Three Times, Etc. [Cardinals of Time]
s.d: a single occurrence{N:001}
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐφάπαξ in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:6|1 Corinthians 15:6⟧, see LN 67.34.

s.dp: Number › Once, Twice, Three Times, Etc. [Cardinals of Time]
s.d: a single occurrence to the exclusion of any other similar occurrence
s.g: once and for all; once and never again
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘once and for all’ is simply ‘once and not again’ or ‘once and not twice.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time which is emphatically simultaneous with another point of time
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐφάπαξ in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:6|1 Corinthians 15:6⟧, see LN 60.67.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Ἔφεσος<SDBG:Ἔφεσος:000000>} ‘Ephesus,’ {D:93.471}) pertaining to Ephesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Ἔφεσος<SDBG:Ἔφεσος:000000>} ‘Ephesus,’ {D:93.471}) a person who lives in or is a native of Ephesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a seaport in the western part of the Roman province of Asia

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: one who thinks up schemes or plans of action
s.g: contriver; inventor; one who thinks up

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a class or division of persons who perform certain daily duties (in the one NT occurrence, a reference to a group of priests performing certain functions in the Temple at Jerusalem)
s.c: It may be necessary to expand somewhat the expression ‘the work group of Abijah’ (⟦Luke 1:5|Luke 1:5⟧) to read ‘a work group known as the division of Abijah.’ Otherwise, one might get the impression that this was a work group under the command of Abijah or a group of persons who belonged specifically to the person named Abijah. If it is difficult to obtain a satisfactory expression for ‘work group,’ one can of course translate the final clause of ⟦Luke 1:5|Luke 1:5⟧ as simply ‘who belonged to a group of priests known as the group of Abijah.’

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: pertaining to recurring on a daily basis

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move toward and to arrive at a point{N:001}
s.g: to come to; to reach; to arrive

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Stand
s.d: to stand at a particular place, often with the implication of suddenness
s.g: to stand by; to stand at
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐφίσταμαι in ⟦Luke 24:4|Luke 24:4⟧, see LN 85.13.

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in proximity to something
s.g: to be near; to be at; to be nearby
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐφίσταμαι in ⟦Luke 24:4|Luke 24:4⟧, see LN 17.5.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to happen to someone or something, with the implication of an event which is undesirable
s.g: to happen to; to come upon; to overtake

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Attack
s.d: to use sudden physical force against someone as the outgrowth of a hostile attitude{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to attack’ is simply ‘to start fighting against.’ In some languages, however, the equivalent is ‘to jump on’ or ‘to grab to do harm to.’|Although according to the Greek text the attack was made on the home of Jason, the actual objects of the attack were the persons in the home. The attack may very well have involved battering down the door, and in some languages it may be necessary to make explicit this aspect of the attack.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: to occur with high probability at a point of time just subsequent to another point of time

s.dp: Aspect › Begin, Start
s.d: to begin, with the focus upon the initial stages of an activity
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἐφίσταμαι in ⟦Acts 28:2|Acts 28:2⟧ as meaning ‘to be imminent’ (see LN 67.63).

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: to continue in an activity in spite of presumed opposition

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city of uncertain location

s.dp: Features of Objects › Open, Closed
s.d: (an Aramaic word)
s.c: The Aramaic word εφφαθα, together with the Greek interpretation ‘be opened,’ may still be relatively meaningless in the context of ⟦Mark 7:34|Mark 7:34⟧ since it refers to the capacity for hearing.|In a number of languages one does not speak of a deaf person as ‘one whose ears are closed.’ The most appropriate equivalent may simply be ‘be able to hear’ or even ‘now you can hear.’

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Opposition, Hostility
s.d: a state of enmity with someone

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Opposition, Hostility
s.d: pertaining to being at enmity with someone
s.g: being an enemy; in opposition to

s.dp: Animals › Reptiles and Other 'Creeping Things'
s.d: kind of poisonous snake; associated with lurking danger
s.c: The terms ἀσπίς and ἔχιδνα may be used to refer to almost any kind of poisonous snake, and since at least some type of poisonous snake occurs in practically all parts of the world, there is usually little difficulty involved in finding an appropriate term. One can, however, always employ a descriptive expression, for example, ‘a snake whose bite causes death.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἔχιδνα<SDBG:ἔχιδνα:000000>}[a] ‘viper,’ {D:4.53}) a dangerous and despised person
s.c: One must exercise due caution in rendering ἔχιδνα in ⟦Matthew 12:34|Matthew 12:34⟧ and ὄφις in ⟦Matthew 23:33|Matthew 23:33⟧, since in some cultures snakes are regarded as being particularly wise and clever, and therefore an expression such as ‘brood of vipers’ could be a compliment. In some languages important distinctions are made between different types of snakes, and therefore connotations may vary considerably.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: to have or possess objects or property (in the technical sense of having control over the use of such objects){N:001}{N:002}
s.g: to have; to own; to possess; to belong to

s.dp: Attachment › Grasp, Hold
s.d: to hold on to an object
s.g: to hold on to; to retain in the hand; to seize

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Have an Opinion, Hold a View
s.d: to hold a view or have an opinion with regard to something
s.g: to hold a view; to have an opinion; to consider; to regard

s.dp: Activities Involving Clothing and Adorning
s.d: to wear clothes

s.dp: Able, Capable
s.d: to possess the capacity to do something
s.g: to be able to; to have the capacity to

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to experience a state or condition, generally involving duration

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to be in a particular state or condition

s.dp: Case › Agent in a Causative Role Marked by Verbs
s.d: a marker of a causative relation, with otherwise almost empty semantic content
s.g: to cause; to bring about; to produce

s.dp: Case › Content
s.d: a marker of designations of content

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Acknowledge
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have in recognition) to recognize something as being what it truly is
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπίγνωσις in ⟦Romans 1:28|Romans 1:28⟧, see LN 28.2.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have in common) to share with one another equitably
s.g: to share; to share with one another
s.c: The mutuality of sharing may be expressed in some languages as ‘each person shared with all of the rest’ or ‘each person gave to the others and received from the others.’

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have a part in) to experience along with others
s.g: to experience together with; to share in experiencing

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Hear
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have ear) to be able to hear, with the implication of being expected to hear or having the obligation to hear (with a further implication of related mental activity)
s.g: to be able to hear; can hear
s.c: In rendering the idiom ἔχω οὖς in ⟦Revelation 2:7|Revelation 2:7⟧, the implication is that the individuals involved ought to be able to hear and pay attention.

s.dp: Communication › Foretell, Tell Fortunes
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have a spirit of python, an appositional construction in Greek) to tell people for pay what would happen to them in the future

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to be at an extreme) to be very sick, with the implication of imminent death
s.g: to be very sick; to be about to die

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have badly, or: to fare badly) to be in a bad state, to be ill
s.g: to be ill; to be sick (to some extent equivalent to the English idiom to be bad off in speaking of ill health)

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Health, Vigor, Strength
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have well) the state of being healthy, well (in contrast with sickness)
s.g: to be well; to be healthy
s.c: In a number of languages health is expressed only in terms of strength, for ‘to be well’ is ‘to be strong.’ In other languages, however, to be well or to be healthy is a negation of illness or sickness, so that in ⟦Mark 16:18|Mark 16:18⟧ one may translate ‘they will place their hands on those who are sick and these people will become not sick.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have bed, though in combination with ἔχω, κοίτη early acquired the metonymic meaning of sexual relations) to be in a state of pregnancy
s.c: This expression contrasts with the meaning of συλλαμβάνω, LN 23.49, in that it seems to focus more upon the state of pregnancy rather than the event of conception.

s.dp: Spacial Positions › At, Beside, Near, Far
s.d: (a participial form of {L:ἔχω<SDBG:ἔχω:000000>}[a] ‘to have,’ {D:57.1}) a position contiguous to another position

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have in the womb) to be in a state of pregnancy
s.c: This expression contrasts with the meaning of συλλαμβάνω, LN 23.49, in that it seems to focus more upon the state of pregnancy rather than the event of conception.|It is impossible to determine whether in ⟦Matthew 1:23|Matthew 1:23⟧ (ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν ‘she will be pregnant and bear a son’) the focus is upon the state of pregnancy or the fact of conception (see LN 23.49).

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: a day immediately following a previous day{N:005}
s.g: the next day; on the next day

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: the continuous extent of time up to a point{N:001}
s.g: until; to; at last; at length
s.c: The phrase εἰ μὴ ὅταν is often translated as ‘until’ (for example, μηδενὶ ἅ εἶδον διηγήσωνταιεἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ ‘not to tell anybody what they have seen until the Son of Man has risen from death’ ⟦Mark 9:9|Mark 9:9⟧), but this phrase may be analyzed as meaning ‘if it is not when,’ an expression which is semantically equivalent to ‘until.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: an extent of time of the same length as another extent or unit of time

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension up to or as far as a goal{N:002}
s.g: to; up to; as far as

s.dp: Degree › Up To, As Much As, To the Degree That [Marked Extent of Degree]
s.d: a degree extending to a particular point as marked by the context
s.g: to the point of; to the extent of; to the degree that; up to
s.c: In a number of languages it is difficult to express in a succinct manner a degree which reaches to a particular point. The same meaning, however, may often be expressed in a somewhat different form. For example, in ⟦Matthew 26:38|Matthew 26:38⟧ one may translate ‘my soul is very sorrowful; it is just as though I were dying.’

s.dp: Quantity › Much, Little [Masses, Collectives, Extensions]
s.d: the extent of a quantity
s.c: In a number of languages it may be necessary to restructure somewhat the expression ‘up to half of my kingdom,’ for example, ‘I will give you half of my kingdom but not more than half.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: an extent of time of the same length as another extent or unit of time

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: an extent of time of the same length as another extent or unit of time

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the territory of the tribe of Zebulun

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a chief tax collector of Jericho

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a priest who was the father of John the Baptist

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: an OT prophet killed in the Temple

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to be in existence, having life, not dead
s.c: In some figurative expressions ζάω and ζωή may involve serious complications in reference. For example, in ⟦John 6:51|John 6:51⟧ the expression ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν ‘I am the living bread’ may be understood in some languages as bread which has some living objects in it, namely, bread which is being eaten by worms or weevils. It may therefore be necessary to say ‘I am that bread which gives life.’|In a number of languages there is no noun-like word for ‘life.’ It may therefore be necessary to change all passages which speak of ‘life’ into a corresponding expression using a verb-like form meaning ‘to live.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to come back to life after having once died
s.g: to come back to life; to live again; to be resurrected; resurrection
s.c: In a number of languages there is a difficulty involved in formulating some expression for ‘resurrection’ or ‘living again,’ since such a phrase may refer to what is technically known as metempsychosis, that is to say, the rebirth of the soul in another existence, a belief which is widely held in a number of areas of south Asia. This problem may be avoided in some languages by speaking of ‘his body will live again’ or ‘his body will come back to life’ or ‘he will be the same person when he lives again.’

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to conduct oneself, with the particular manner specified by the context
s.g: to live; to conduct oneself; to behave
s.c: In ⟦2 Timothy 3:12|2 Timothy 3:12⟧ ζάω does not refer to physiological existence, but rather to the manner in which a person behaves or conducts himself in relationship to other persons and to God.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of the apostles James and John
